title: Miso-Glazed Salmon
subtitle: Salmon fillets baked under a sweet white miso and mirin glaze
excerpt: The miso glaze takes five minutes to mix and gives the salmon a lacquered, deeply savoury crust in the oven. This is one of the fastest weeknight fish dishes you can make.
sourceNotes: Nobu Matsuhisa popularised miso-glazed black cod in the 1990s, inspiring home cooks to apply the same treatment to salmon. White miso is milder and sweeter than red, making it well suited to fish.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Marinate the salmon in the glaze for up to 24 hours in the fridge for a deeper flavour.
recipe.temperatureNote: Fan 180C / Gas 6. Switch to the grill for the final 2 minutes if you want a darker crust.

content.text: Miso burns quickly because of its sugar content. Watch the salmon in the last 2 minutes of cooking and switch the oven to grill only if you want extra colour on top.
Mix together all the glaze ingredients in a small bowl until smooth.
Pat the salmon dry. Place in the roasting tin. Spread the glaze evenly over the top and sides of each fillet.
Leave to marinate for at least 30 minutes in the fridge. Bring to room temperature 10 minutes before cooking.
Preheat the oven. Bake for 10 to 12 minutes until the salmon is just cooked through. The glaze should be caramelised and slightly blistered.
Rest for 2 minutes. Serve with steamed rice and cucumber or green vegetables.

items.symptom: The glaze has burnt and turned bitter.
items.cause: The oven temperature was too high or the fish was too close to the grill.
items.fix: Reduce to 180C and keep the tin on the middle shelf.

items.symptom: The salmon is overcooked and dry.
items.cause: It was left in too long.
items.fix: Check at 9 minutes; salmon is done when it flakes with light pressure.

items.symptom: The glaze slid off during cooking.
items.cause: The salmon was wet when the glaze was applied.
items.fix: Always pat dry before glazing; moisture breaks the adhesion.
